lessons.title: Mutex for Coroutine-Safe Shared State
lessons.content: @Synchronized blocks a whole OS thread, which is wasteful with coroutines that may be running on a shared thread pool - it can even deadlock a dispatcher. Mutex is coroutine-aware: withLock suspends the coroutine instead of blocking the thread, letting other coroutines use that thread while waiting. Real scenario: an in-memory cache being written to from multiple concurrent network callbacks - Mutex ensures only one coroutine mutates the cache map at a time without blocking threads.

lessons.title: Channels & select for Producer-Consumer Patterns
lessons.content: A Channel is like a coroutine-safe BlockingQueue - one coroutine sends, another receives, and it suspends instead of blocking on both ends. `select` lets a coroutine wait on multiple suspending operations simultaneously and react to whichever completes first. Real scenario: a background sync worker reading from multiple sources (local DB changes channel, remote push notification channel) and reacting to whichever event arrives first.
